grades.quote: For exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes, the corresponding `medeleg` bits should be read-only zero. In particular, `medeleg` [11] is read-only zero.
grades.reason: Describes medeleg bit layout (index = mcause value) and says bits for exceptions that cannot occur in less-privileged modes are read-only zero (e.g., bits 11 and 16), so those cannot be delegated. This is part of the answer. It does not explicitly say to write ones and read back to discover delegatable bits.
Covers virtualizing scountovf under Smcdeleg. It has nothing to do with discovering which exceptions medeleg can delegate.
This table gives hedeleg bit attributes (writable vs read-only 0) for delegation from HS-mode to VS-mode. The query asks about medeleg delegating to S-mode, so the table is for the wrong register.

grades.quote: Guest-page-fault traps may be delegated from M-mode to HS-mode under the control of CSR `medeleg` , but cannot be delegated to other privilege modes.
grades.reason: Says guest-page faults can be delegated from M-mode to HS-mode via medeleg and no further. This tells software about one exception class's delegatability, but it gives no general way to discover which exceptions medeleg can delegate.
